findings.issue: Options-only pass scored 178/200 (89%), above the 82% ceiling: about 50 items have wrong options that are false on their face (absurd or off-topic), so a candidate with no Singapore-specific knowledge picks the key. Worst items: LAW-001, LAW-010, LAW-013, GRD-003, GRD-005, GRD-006, GRD-009, GRD-010, GRD-012, GRD-025, EQP-001, EQP-002, EQP-003, PAT-001, PAT-002, PAT-004, PAT-005, PAT-011, PAT-012, PAT-015, PAT-016, PAT-019, PAT-025, PAT-026, CRM-001, CRM-003, CRM-007, CRM-008, CRM-009, CRM-011, CRM-016, CRM-018, CRM-020, CRM-024, TER-001, TER-004, TER-012, TER-014, TER-015, TER-016, TER-017, TER-029, TER-032, FIR-002, FIR-010, AID-004, AID-008, AID-017, AID-018, AID-019.
findings.fix: Rewrite the distractors of these items as plausible, parallel wrong answers in the same domain (e.g. LAW-001: other non-licensable tasks that sound like security work such as 'Monitoring a building's fire alarm panel as a technician', 'Working as a car park attendant collecting fees', 'Acting as a concierge'; GRD-025: plausible wrong first steps such as 'Report to the Control Room before speaking to them', 'Record it in the Occurrence Book first'; TER-004: other genuine-sounding but non-listed methods). Do not change keys; re-run options_only after rewriting.

findings.issue: 'Safe move' pattern: in many safety and conduct items the key is the only cautious option and the other three are reckless (film the fire, carry the burning e-scooter out, hang up and run, negotiate with attackers). Keys are correct per SCDF/PLRD, but the pick needs no knowledge. Items: GRD-002, GRD-026, PAT-009, PAT-013, CRM-013, CRM-015, FIR-007, FIR-013, FIR-015, FIR-021, TER-018, TER-021, TER-024, TER-028, AID-020.
findings.fix: Make at least two distractors cautious-but-wrong (e.g. FIR-015: 'Use a dry powder extinguisher on the battery', 'Cover it with a fire blanket'; TER-024: 'Transfer the call to the supervisor', 'Ask the caller to call 999 instead'), so the item tests the specific procedure, not general prudence.

findings.issue: Content-validity: stem asks who needs the X-ray machine certificate; key 'One running a bag X-ray machine' repeats the stem's words. Answerable with no knowledge.
findings.fix: Ask instead which certification a walk-through/handheld metal detector or X-ray operator needs (names of the two screening certificates as options), or whether a Grade can do functions above it.

findings.issue: Key 'A prompt response to her' is the only non-negligent option; reg 7A(1)(e) fact not actually tested.
findings.fix: Offer plausible wrong limits (e.g. 'only if she is injured', 'only after informing the Control Room and waiting for instructions').

findings.issue: Stem logic decides it ('on a break... phone rings'): 'Answer it promptly' vs let it ring/unplug.
findings.fix: Rewrite with plausible alternatives (e.g. who should answer, how to greet, what to record).

findings.issue: Key 'Seize it and detain him' matches PLRD's scenario answer; note that legally a private person's arrest rests on CPC s 66 (arrestable non-bailable offence in view, or s 66(6) offence against the victim's property with name/address unknown). Missing gate pass alone may not be theft; explanation could mention handing over to police without delay.
findings.fix: Optional: add 'as PLRD's procedure sets out' to the stem or explanation.

landing_findings.issue: Description opens 'Free practice for...'; exam has Premium steps (last 25% locked). House rule: say free to start, never imply all is free (title may keep 'Free').
landing_findings.fix: 'Free-to-start practice for...' or end with 'Free to start.'

landing_findings.issue: 'must pass before PLRD grants a security officer licence': PLRD FAQ and SPF PWM page frame the four units as required before deployment; elsewhere the page and examFacts say 'before being deployed'.
landing_findings.fix: Use 'before being deployed under a security officer licence'.

landing_findings.issue: Checked against PLRD FAQ, licensing conditions, refresher package and PSIA ss 17A-17E: units, 1 Jan 2024 start, 31 Dec 2026 deadline, no published count/pass mark, refresher e-quiz, s 23 five-year validity all consistent. s 13 and s 24 text could not be re-read (SSO throttled with 202/403); keys LAW-001, LAW-005..009 rely on the builder's quoted text.
